correctness.rationale: For a vertex pair the two arc totals are A and R-A, giving A(R-A)/R. Each edge pair at distance d contributes its product once for each vertex pair separated by deleting those two edges, giving d(n-d) occurrences. Expanding r_i=1+delta I_i gives the frozen expression with strictly positive placement coefficient delta^2/(n+k delta). In the spacing simplex each directed block length L contributes L(n-L), with an overall factor 1/2; the length-one terms ensure strict concavity, so only the simplex vertices minimize and they are all rotations of the clustered block. For maxima, each fixed block length has fixed sum and smoothing two differing integer lengths by one improves the quadratic unless all lengths differ by at most one. Floor placements attain every block bound simultaneously. The residues ell*n mod k repeat g times across the multiples of g, giving the claimed gcd correction. The contrast is positive since n-k>=2 and g>=1, giving a bracket at least 3(k^2-1)>0. Symmetric jump rates give uniform stationary weights and the Laplacian pseudoinverse gives K/n for stationary-target hitting time (zero for the starting target). Independent replay python3 -B /workspace/reproductions/5.py checks 16028 exact resistance cases with two different contrasts and 12 cases with all-target rational hitting-time systems; universal results follow from the algebra.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The balance criteria are equivalent: if the lengths between ell-th successive ones differ by at least two, a bin of length one more than the shorter distance can contain ell+1 ones in the dense region and at most ell-1 starting just after the first endpoint of the longer distance. Conversely if equal-length bins of length L contain at least p+2 and at most p ones, the (p+1)-th-next-one distances are at most L-1 in the first and at least L+1 starting just before the second. Thus the earlier two equality cases transfer exactly.
